value_per_capex_dollar.note: a year's demonstrated alloys valued at what the conventional lab pays for one (its full cost per alloy), plus outside users' net revenue, over the vertical lab's capex

assumptions: Prices: procurement records and list prices where cited in econ.py's tables; estimates and assumptions marked so (zwickiLine, MX-Lab installation, fit-out, couplings, the CubXL bundle, hoods).

Depreciation straight-line over 5-20 years (BYU capitalizes equipment over 3-10 years, buildings over 40); service contracts 2-10 % of the price a year (8-15 % for full service on analytical instruments).

Labour: the conventional lab's hands-on hours per booking (econ.HANDS_ON, assumed) at a BYU PhD student's stipend and tuition over 1,500 research hours; the vertical lab's one day-shift technician (upkeep.py) and a quarter of a research engineer, at BLS Provo-Orem means plus an assumed 35 % fringe. Design and analysis time is excluded from both.

The conventional lab's in-house stations that the twin leaves free (Instron frames, hardness, metallography) carry no charge; BYU's internal core-facility rates are subsidised (BYU EM: operating cost about $300/h).

Outside work: catalogue rates from published user-facility rate sheets; demand is not modelled beyond a cap and an assumed 20 h a week per instrument; handling 0.25 h of a technician and 10 % consumables a job.
